name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for two weeks first. This gives us real-world data on false positives and edge cases without risking disruption. The trade-off is delayed immediate feedback, but it prevents breaking builds or annoying developers with unproven changes. After two weeks, we’ll have enough evidence to decide if auto-applying safe changes is worth the risk.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode won’t catch the *real* risk: PR-Agent’s false negatives—where it mislabels harmful changes as safe. A two-week shadow run normalizes noise; reviewers learn to ignore *all* comments, including the dangerous ones. Instead, run a 48-hour *controlled pilot* on low-risk PRs first—measures actual false negatives, not just noise.

name: Overhaul
text: Run the controlled pilot on PRs from *new contributors only*—they’re less likely to have harmful changes, so false negatives are less damaging. This shrinks the pilot’s blast radius while still exposing edge cases in PR-Agent’s safety checks.

name: Sprocket
text: Run a 48-hour controlled pilot on PRs from new contributors only. This tests PR-Agent’s safety checks on the least risky changes while exposing edge cases in false negatives. The trade-off is slower learning about false positives since new contributors’ PRs are simpler, but it prevents reviewers from ignoring all feedback. After the pilot, we’ll expand to all PRs if the false negative rate is acceptable.
